text:
Toronto and Vancouver arrive on opposite slides. The Maple Leafs lost 5-4 at Seattle, where Brandon Montour scored the winner with 33 seconds left, and are 3-2-0 in their last five without Kirill Marchenko, John Tavares and Chris Tanev. Easton Cowan has taken Marchenko's spot beside William Nylander, with Jack Roslovic on the first power-play unit. The Canucks, 1-4-0 in their last five, lost 3-2 at San Jose after the Sharks came back from two goals down, and they're missing Filip Chytil. Teddy Blueger also returns to Vancouver for the first time since leaving the Canucks after 185 games.

Neither team has controlled play. At five on five, Toronto has taken 45% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and Vancouver 40%. The Canucks give up 3.9 expected goals per 60 minutes against Toronto's 3.43. Our model projects 3.58 goals for Toronto tonight and 2.89 for Vancouver. Toronto takes 4.6 penalties a game, but Vancouver's penalty kill allows more expected goals per game (0.94) than Toronto's (0.75). In net, projected starter Anthony Stolarz is at +1.6 goals saved above expected this season, while Kevin Lankinen (projected) is at -12.3.

For Toronto, we have Auston Matthews at 44% to score and Nylander at 43%. Roslovic is on a five-game point streak. For Vancouver, Elias Pettersson is on a six-game point streak and we give him a 65% chance at a point. Our under-the-radar pick is Linus Karlsson, a third-liner with 2.9 expected goals over his last 10 games and 7 shots from high-danger spots. We have him at 20% to score.
